transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-09 14:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood CSM), Samantha Reed (Aurora Head of MLOps), Tom Bennett (Aurora VP Eng), Renee Cho (Aurora Security)

Summary section (auto-generated): Brief recap of incident, timeline, and actions.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all squeezing this in, uh we wanted to run through the postmortem and make sure the mitigations we've pushed are holding and to align on the pilot next steps
[00:14] Samantha: yeah thanks jordan, um quick note our on-call was still seeing intermittent 502s yesterday morning but much lower frequency than the main incident so kicking off here to confirm root cause and next steps
[00:28] Priya: just to be clear for context, root cause we tracked to a KV cache invalidation race during a burst of warmup traffic after a deploy, combined with VPC peering ratelimit on aurora's side, that exacerbated the token generation retries, so two things together not one single fault
[00:46] Tom: right and the network team saw a spike in connection resets between our peering and the redwood private endpoint, looked like short TCP resets, probably transient but overlapped with the cache miss storm
[01:03] Renee: for security i just want to confirm that no PII left our VPC, yes? we saw logs showing requests stayed in-region and ephemerally cached, correct?
[01:18] Priya: yes based on the traces we reviewed, requests were routed to your dedicated private endpoints, data did not exit your VPC, cache was ephemeral and TTL short, but i will attach the trace snippets to the postmortem doc (sorry transcription of some trace IDs may be messy)
[01:37] Miguel: quick status: we pushed the emergency mitigation saturday night, increased cache TTL a tick and added a short backoff on retries plus temporary rate-limit shadow to smooth bursts, that reduced error rate from ~12% to under 0.7% across affected routes
[01:55] Samantha: we saw that improvement in our dashboards, thanks. can you walk through what the permanent fix is?
[02:08] Priya: permanent path is two-fold: one, fix the invalidation ordering in the KV cache write path in runtime (we have a patch in review), two, adjust batching and pre-warm heuristics to avoid simultaneous cold-starts. third is network hardening: work with aurora network to adjust peering idle timeouts and increase allowable connection rate for the Dedicated pilot
[02:33] Jordan: is going to clarify pilot options: Dedicated reserved capacity gives you isolated pools and predictable throughput which helps with these burst patterns, and also reduces incidence of noisy-neighbor effects on shared endpoints
[02:46] Tom: curious tradeoffs on cost, is Dedicated overprovisioned? what are the auto-scale behaviors?
[02:57] Jordan: we can do committed reserved with burst capacity; pricing is per-GPU-hour plus throughput credits. auto-scale can be configured with margin targets so you don't overcommit but still hit the SLO. i'll send a pricing matrix after this meeting
[03:14] Renee: on compliance, we need the KMS integration details and audit log retention levels, SOC2 artifact set, and would like confirmation on RBAC within the control plane
[03:28] Miguel: we'll share the security pack, KMS integration steps, and RBAC docs. renee if you want a deeper session with our security lead we can schedule that next week
[03:44] Samantha: yes please. also curious about the planned timeline for the runtime patch
[03:50] Priya: patch is in code review now, target deploy to a canary fleet by 2026-09-14, and global rollout 2026-09-21 if canary metrics look good. we will run targeted tests to validate invalidation ordering and add extra assertions in the CI e2e tests
[04:12] Tom: what about the KV cache tuning you mentioned? any numbers we can expect for p99 latency improvement?
[04:20] Priya: initial lab runs show p99 token latency improvement of about 20% when we avoid the invalidation storm, and error rate drop to <1%. but real-world depends on your sequence length distribution and concurrency; we'll run the VPC load test against your sample traces
[04:38] Samantha: could you do that test in our account using our sample traffic?
[04:42] Priya: yep, need temporary credentials and a small config change to point the runner at your endpoints, and we will run a couple scenarios (steady-state, bursty ramp, and mixed)
[04:55] Jordan: adding a note, were fine to do it as a timeboxed pilot with Dedicated capacity for the run; that will give representative numbers for P99 and cost per 1k tokens
[05:09] Renee: if we do Dedicated pilot we will need answers to legal questions before we hand credentials, procurement will need the MSA and an SOC2 cert copy
[05:23] Miguel: i'll coordinate procurement doc bundle and connect legal/procurement contacts
[05:30] [crosstalk briefly]
[05:36] Samantha: on the mitigations you pushed, any risk of regressions from the increased TTL? like stale context surfacing?
[05:45] Priya: good point, we increased TTL slightly as a stop-gap which could risk serving slightly stale prefixes for longer windows; that's why we prefer the ordering fix and smarter pre-warm heuristics rather than relying on long TTLs longer term
[06:03] Tom: do we have a rollback plan if the canary shows unexpected behavior?
[06:08] Priya: yes canary will be on 10% of traffic for 48 hours with automatic rollback if error rate or latency thresholds exceed defined SLOs; we keep flaky feature flags to revert changes quickly
[06:23] Jordan: i'll document the thresholds and share them in the postmortem doc, and we can align on acceptable SLO numbers for aurora
[06:34] Miguel: action item recap coming up, but i want to surface a reliability suggestion from our infra team: add explicit connection pooling and keepalive tuning on the VPC egress side to reduce transient resets, that helped a different customer once
[06:52] Samantha: we'll have our infra team try that as part of the network changes with our cloud provider
[07:01] Priya: for the VPC load tests we plan two runs: one on your current shared endpoints and one against a Dedicated pool with pre-warm, to compare p50/p95/p99 and error profiles. we'll attach raw CSVs and graphs to the postmortem doc
[07:23] Tom: timeline wise when can we see the first test results?
[07:27] Priya: target by 2026-09-16, i.e. within a week after the canary deploy. we'll also include a diff showing the KV cache hit rates and retry counts
[07:40] Renee: can you include a short writeup about what we should expect from audit logs (fields, retention, how to map to our SIEM)
[07:47] Miguel: yes, security bundle will include sample audit log schema and retention options
[07:55] Jordan: ok want to surface one risk, if your traffic pattern has extremely bursty short-lived clients the initial cold-start will still be a hard problem; batching and pre-warm help but Dedicated pilot will be the clearest way to validate cost/latency tradeoffs
[08:11] Samantha: understood, pilot scope then should include the 3 most critical routes and the realtime chat endpoint
[08:19] Jordan: perfect, we'll propose a pilot scope doc after the call
[08:25] [15:00] (mid-call notes, transcription jumps)
[15:01] Priya: attaching: canary plan, patch diff, test harness, and runbook changes. we'll also add extra alarms for cache invalidation anomalies
[15:17] Tom: on runbooks, our SREs want step-by-step for identifying a cache-invalidation storm and recommended immediate mitigations to reduce user impact
[15:31] Priya: we'll add a new runbook page "detecting and mitigating KV-invalidation storms" with exact queries and playbook steps (disable invalidate, increase backoff, scale Dedicated pool)
[15:46] Samantha: ok that sounds good. can you also provide an exec summary we can paste into our incident report?
[15:52] Miguel: yes i'll prepare a 1-page exec summary and the full timeline w/ timestamps and owners
[16:03] Jordan: any other security blockers?
[16:06] Renee: just the KMS integration detail and confirmation that logs are accessible for our auditors for 365 days, and that RBAC separates billing/control plane from runtime access
[16:19] Miguel: we have options for 365-day retention as an add-on, will include that in the procurement bundle
[16:30] Samantha: timeline recap?
[16:32] Priya: canary deploy 2026-09-14, run tests 2026-09-16, target global rollout 2026-09-21, pilot scope confirmed by 2026-09-14, security docs 2026-09-12, postmortem doc 2026-09-11
[16:51] Jordan: great, we'll close with next steps and owners, i'll send the pricing and pilot doc by monday
[17:00] Miguel: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the postmortem bundle and assign action items in the doc tracker
[17:08] Samantha: thanks all, appreciate the quick response and the follow up plan
[17:12] [END]
